title: Adversarial Red-Team & Kill Switch Pattern
description: A pattern combining pre-launch adversarial red-teaming (specifically simulating coordinated manipulation attempts) with a tested, rehearsed kill-switch mechanism for a publicly-facing AI system that adapts its behaviour from live input.
problem: A publicly-facing AI system that learns or adapts from live user input can be deliberately manipulated by coordinated bad-faith actors faster than a manual monitoring process can detect and respond, especially if there is no pre-rehearsed way to disable the system quickly.
solution: Before launch, run adversarial red-team exercises specifically simulating coordinated manipulation (not just individual bad prompts), and build and rehearse a kill-switch or rollback procedure capable of disabling the system within minutes — tested as an actual drill, not just documented as a plan.
applicability: Any publicly-facing AI system that adapts its behaviour from live, unmoderated user input, particularly conversational agents on open platforms.
consequences: Red-teaming can only anticipate known categories of manipulation and will not catch every novel attack; an easily-triggered kill-switch also creates an availability risk if triggered by a false alarm or a bad actor seeking to disrupt the service.

relationships.reason: A tested kill-switch and rollback plan is the concrete mechanism satisfying this control.
The pattern's output is a red-team test report.
